data.label: SSI claim (Title XVI application / recipient record)

receipts.basis: Computer Matching Agreement, SSA Match #1016 / IRS Project #066 (DIFSLA), fully executed Oct 20 2025, effective Jan 1 2026 – Jun 30 2027. Under IRC § 6103(l)(7) the IRS discloses unearned-income information from the Information Returns Master File to SSA; SSA submits an SSN-based finder file (from the Supplemental Security Record), IRS matches it against information returns (e.g. Form 1099) and returns unearned-income records; SSA uses the result to verify SSI (Title XVI) eligibility and correct benefit amounts. FY2023 cost-benefit: ~$74.5M projected SSI benefit from overpayments recovered and ongoing payments corrected. (Paraphrase: the SSA-hosted PDF blocks automated retrieval; facts corroborated by the SSA CMA index and IRS IRM 11.3.29.)

IRS Internal Revenue Manual 11.3.29 (DIFSLA): "Pursuant to IRC 6103(l)(7)(B), the IRS shall disclose unearned income information from the IRMF [Information Returns Master File] to federal, state, and local agencies administering the federal benefit programs pursuant to the DIFSLA program." Recipient agencies may use the information "only to determine eligibility or to correct amount of benefits" and may not redisclose it to contractors; detailed request procedures are in IRS Publication 3373.

Federal Register notice of the SSA/IRS computer matching program, Match #1016 (Nov 16 2000): the IRS discloses return information to SSA to verify Title XVI (SSI) eligibility and/or correct benefit amounts for aged, blind, and disabled individuals — establishing the unearned-income match that the current CMA re-establishes. Cited for lineage (the match has recurred since 2000).

contestation.notice: Privacy Act matching notice published in the Federal Register (SSA/IRS Match #1016)
contestation.appeal: CMPPA, 5 U.S.C. 552a(p): SSA must independently verify and give notice + a 30-day chance to contest before any adverse action

receipts.basis: 26 U.S.C. § 6103(l)(7) directs the Secretary of the Treasury to disclose return information with respect to unearned income to federal, state, and local agencies administering specified federally-assisted benefit programs — including Supplemental Security Income (Title XVI of the Social Security Act). AUTHORIZES the disclosure; it does not, by itself, witness the match (the CMA does).

Computer Matching and Privacy Protection Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552a(p): an agency may not suspend, terminate, reduce, or make a final denial of a benefit to an individual as a result of information produced by a matching program until the agency has independently verified the information and provided the individual notice and a 30-day opportunity to contest. This is the statutory verify-before-adverse-action safeguard cited in the edge contestation blocks.

contestation.notice: SSA notice of the income discrepancy found by the match
contestation.appeal: recipient may contest before SSI is reduced or suspended; SSA must independently verify the IRS data first (CMPPA)

cases.title: IRS/SSA DIFSLA (Match #1016) — SSI recipients matched against IRS unearned-income records
cases.headline: How SSI recipients become an IRS income match
cases.dek: SSA sends recipient identifiers to the IRS, which matches them against information-return records and returns unearned-income data used to verify SSI eligibility and benefit amounts — a written computer matching agreement, not an inference.
cases.why: This is documented composition: a benefit recipient's identifier is joined to IRS income records by agreement, and the result can reduce or recover their payment. The same match has recurred since 2000, with a statutory safeguard requiring SSA to verify and notice before any adverse action.
